facts.raw_span: 3-year history of a complex progressive disorder
Emotional lability
Cognitive decline
Generalized ataxia
Autonomic dysfunction
Patient denied paresthesias, dysesthesias, or loss of sensation
Abnormal cardiac parasympathetic function (without orthostatic hypotension)
Patchy decrease in sweat output on quantitative sudomotor axon reflex test
Markedly abnormal thermoregulatory sweat test with near complete global anhidrosis
α-galactosidase activity: 0.056 U/L (normal range: 0.074-0.457 U/L)
Elevated protein levels (95 mg/dL) in cerebrospinal fluid analysis
Bilateral hyperintensity in the pulvinar region of thalami and global diffuse brain volume loss on MRI Brain

concepts.why: The patient's low alpha-galactosidase activity, abnormal thermoregulatory sweat test, and bilateral hyperintensity in the pulvinar region of thalami are consistent with Fabry disease.

concepts.why: The patient's generalized ataxia, autonomic dysfunction, and abnormal autonomic testing are consistent with multiple system atrophy, but the low alpha-galactosidase activity suggests an alternative diagnosis.

rationales.F09: Markedly abnormal thermoregulatory sweat test with near complete global anhidrosis is highly suggestive of Fabry disease
rationales.F10: Low α-galactosidase activity is a key diagnostic feature of Fabry disease
rationales.F05: Autonomic dysfunction is a common feature of both Fabry disease and multiple system atrophy
rationales.F07: Abnormal cardiac parasympathetic function is seen in both Fabry disease and multiple system atrophy
rationales.F08: Patchy decrease in sweat output is consistent with both Fabry disease and multiple system atrophy

frontier_selector.why: The low α-galactosidase activity and the presence of a pseudo-α-galactosidase allele specifically support Fabry disease.
